name: shipments
title: Shipments
description: What physically moved. An order says what is OWED; a shipment says what left the building -- when, in which box, with which tracking number -- and the two are different facts that small systems collapse into one status field and then cannot uncollapse. Partial fulfillment is the proof: it is not a flag on the order, it is a COUNT of shipments, and the order's status is DERIVED from shipment lines by system_order_fulfillment (docs/logic-decisions.md #1: the quantities are the facts, the order status is the read). Everything else the warehouse asks for falls out of this noun as a view -- a packing slip is one shipment printed, a manifest is today's shipments folded by carrier, a pick list is what is not on a shipment yet. ship_to_name/ship_to_address are STAMPED from the order at creation and never re-read: an address is what it was when the box left, and a customer who moves house next month must not silently rewrite where last month's parcel went. direction carries the return case (plan/fulfillment-logistics-spec.md): an RMA is this same document with the sign reversed, which is why there is no separate returns collection -- the authorized status and the disposition flow are a later slice, deliberately absent here rather than half-present.

fields.name: order_id
fields.label: Order
fields.help: The order this shipment is against, and the provenance link every derived status walks back along. Set once at creation and not intended to change after -- not schema read_only for the same reason order_lines.order_id is not: a required, client-submitted-at-creation field cannot also be read_only on this platform.

fields.name: direction
fields.label: Direction
fields.help: outbound is goods leaving us; inbound is a customer return coming back (an RMA IS a shipment with the sign reversed, which is why there is no separate returns collection). Only outbound moves stock today -- system_order_fulfillment skips inbound entirely, because a return that has not been dispositioned yet has not decided whether it is restock or waste, and guessing would put damaged goods back on the shelf.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.help: open -> packed -> shipped -> in_transit -> delivered is the full ladder, and shipped -> delivered directly is deliberately allowed as well: a shop that hands parcels to a driver and never touches a tracking API would otherwise have to fake an in_transit it never observed, and fake precision is worse than a short ladder. packed -> open is the repacking move (the box was opened again before it left; nothing has physically happened yet, so nothing needs compensating). Nothing moves BACK from shipped: once it has left the dock the correction is a new document -- a return is an inbound shipment referencing this one, never an edit to this row (docs/logic-decisions.md #3). delivered, returned_to_sender and lost are terminal. Stock moves are composed when this reaches shipped, once per line, idempotent by provenance marker.

fields.name: carrier
fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Free text on purpose. A carrier list is a connector's job (plan/fulfillment-logistics-spec.md's label boundary), and until credentials exist the honest field is the one the packer can type 'my brother-in-law's van' into.

fields.name: service
fields.label: Service
fields.help: The carrier service level -- 'shipment types' in the warehouse's own words. pickup and digital are here because they are real fulfillment methods that never touch a carrier, and a shipment noun that could not express them would push those sales back into the untracked hand-wave the whole package exists to replace.

fields.name: tracking_number
fields.label: Tracking Number
fields.help: Typed by hand today; written by the label connector when one is configured. Manual-first is the point: the flow works fully without carrier credentials.

fields.name: tracking_status
fields.label: Tracking Status
fields.help: The carrier's own last words about this parcel, kept as text rather than folded into status: their vocabulary is theirs and changes without asking us, and mapping it into our enum is a decision the tracking poll makes explicitly (a later slice) rather than a coincidence of string equality.

fields.name: label_file_id
fields.label: Label File
fields.help: The label PDF, stored as a file the same way a scanned receipt is: evidence posture (docs/logic-decisions.md #8). Blank on every manual shipment, which is most of them.

fields.name: ship_to_name
fields.label: Ship To
fields.help: STAMPED from the order at creation, never re-read from the customer record. An address is what it was when the box left; re-deriving it would let somebody moving house rewrite where last month's parcel went (docs/logic-decisions.md #1).

fields.name: ship_to_address
fields.label: Ship To Address
fields.help: Stamped, for the same reason as ship_to_name. Blank when the order carried no address field at all -- the storefront does not collect one yet, and a shipment that says nothing is honest where a shipment that invents a plausible address is not.

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Notes
fields.help: Also where the provenance marker lands ('Generated by action_create_shipment [orders/{id}]'), the same house pattern app-shop's checkout uses for the invoices it raises.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.label: Entity
fields.help: The set of books this belongs to (65 multi-entity). Optional during rollout, same posture as stock_moves.entity_id.
